props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether several panels may be open at once. When false, opening one item closes the others.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual dressing. `default` is the stroked container with a hard shadow; `plain` drops the container chrome for an accordion that sits inside a card — mirror of sk-card's `bare` reasoning.

props.name: heading
props.description: The summary text.  A `<span>` inside the `<summary>`, not a heading element: the item does not know what level it sits at in the document outline, and a hard-coded heading inside it contradicts the surrounding structure (sk-card's stated reason for the same shape).

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the panel is expanded. Mirrors `<details open>` and is reflected: a consumer can author `<sk-accordion-item open>` in HTML — including server-rendered markup for an already-expanded item — and the attribute tracks what the browser did on a user toggle, so the parent can close siblings and the consumer can read the real state.

ai.summary: A stack of disclosure panels where one, or several, can be open at a time.
whenToUse: Secondary content belongs on the page but should not occupy it — questions, advanced settings, release notes
The reader opens panels in any order and may want none of them open
The content is short enough to expand in place rather than to open a route
whenNotToUse: The sections are the page's navigation — use Tabs
The content must be read in order, or hiding it loses the thread — keep it on the page
Every panel starts open and none should close — use headings and sections
ai.accessibility: Built on the native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements, so the disclosure semantics, the focus stop, the expanded state, and Enter and Space are the browser's rather than reimplemented — which is why the item needs no ARIA of its own. The marker is aria-hidden and drawn with pseudo-elements. `heading` renders as a span inside the summary; a consumer that needs a real heading level puts one in the slot. The summary meets `--sk-touch-min`.
ai.example:
A token layer, a universal package, and framework adapters.

No.
knownLimitations: Exclusive by default: opening an item closes its siblings, and `multiple` opts out
No group-level event summarises the open items — each item dispatches its own bubbling `sk-open-change` with `detail.open`
